transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lynda Kenyon.
President Trump is pledging to send a one-time payment of $90 to seniors
to help them pay their Medicare premiums.
The pledge comes as the cost of living is a major issue for voters
less than five weeks until Election Day.
NPR's Frank Langford reports.
Trump announced Friday the checks would go to more than 20 million Medicare Part B enrollees.
In a video, he said the money would arrive soon in people's bank accounts.
You'll get your money almost immediately.
In everything we do, we're looking out for America's people and America's seniors
and putting more money in your pockets.
Trump said he'll use money from the government's Medicare Improvement Fund.
But according to the Congressional Budget Office, that money is only supposed to be used
to improve the original Medicare program.
Last month, Trump promised American adults $5,000 each
if Republicans keep control of the House and Senate in the midterms.
Polls in recent weeks show 60% of those polled disapprove of the job Trump's doing.
Frank Langford, NPR News, Washington.
Leaders of G7 countries have agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil
and refined products over the next four months.
As NPR's Julia Simon reports, this is especially important for global diesel markets.
In recent weeks, diesel prices have reached record highs,
pushed up by shortages and damage to refineries in the Middle East and Russia
as Ukrainian drone strikes continue to hit Russian refineries.
Last month, diesel topped $6.50 a gallon here in the U.S.
For context, diesel was around $3.75 in September of last year.
That's more than 70% lower.
Diesel prices are even higher in some European countries.
Earlier, President Trump had threatened to cut off U.S. diesel exports,
which both American oil companies and European leaders opposed.
Julia Simon, NPR News.
Multiple data centers are planned for Louisiana, over at U.S.
with the Gulf States newsroom, reports community colleges are preparing locals for new jobs.
At Louisiana Delta Community College in Monroe,
about a dozen students are learning to build and maintain data centers.
I'm going to pass around some safety glasses.
Local businesses often rely on community colleges
to provide the training people need to work for them.
In Northeast Louisiana, the biggest business right now is meta.
The tech giant is building its largest data center here,
and it needs thousands of workers.
Since January, more than 100 people have graduated from Delta's new programs,
which they launched with meta support.
The college says all of the graduates are working.
Some thought they'd have to leave the area to find work
and say they're glad to have an option closer to home.
For NPR News, I'm Aubrey Uhas.
This is NPR.
Two new islands have appeared off the coast of Indonesia's Krakatoa volcano.
Nainu Rao reports this comes after a 25-hour eruption early last month.
The formations sit less than a mile off opposite sides of the volcano,
almost on a straight line through the volcano's crater.
That's according to Indonesia's Geological Agency,
which said that both were discovered weeks after the eruption
by mariners and volunteers who sailed through the area.
While officials cannot definitively confirm the origin
or composition of the islands,
their preliminary assessment said relatively fluid magma released
during the eruption surfaced through an opening.
An erupted material formed these two island-like mounds offshore.
Last month's eruption disrupted thousands of flights
as volcanic ash reached heights of 50,000 feet.
For NPR News, I'm Nainu Rao in Jakarta, Indonesia.
State officials across the U.S. are focusing on rising gas and diesel prices
while the war continues against Iran.
Some states have been offering gas tax holidays
as affordability remains a top concern among voters ahead of the midterms.
About one-third of states are implementing some form of fuel tax relief.
Some have suspended their fuel taxes altogether,
while others have temporarily reduced fuel taxes.
Some states have offered relief but only to farmers and loggers
and some others who use a special type of diesel fuel.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
